Sunlight fell across the public library as three robots prepared in whispered motors. Alpha (id alpha) stood at the front desk (front_desk), where the rare manuscript (rare_manuscript) rested under a glass dome. Beta (id beta) hummed at the charging pod (charge_pod), the library’s only charging station, and Gamma (id gamma) waited in the archive room (archive_room). Their mission: carry the manuscript to the archive room, no matter what. Each robot had strict territory. Alpha could only work between the front desk and the reading hall (reading_hall). Beta moved between the reading hall and the charging pod. Gamma shuttled only between the charging pod and the archive room. The library’s connections shaped the route: the archive room connects to the charging pod; the charging pod connects to the archive room, the reading hall, and the restoration lab (restoration_lab); the front desk connects to the reading hall; the reading hall connects to the charging pod, the front desk, and the restoration lab; the restoration lab connects to the charging pod, the reading hall, and the book return bin (return_bin); and the return bin connects back to the restoration lab. They knew the risk: the first handover of the manuscript from Beta to Gamma might fumble, so they would retry immediately.
